answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may vote on a task’s result. If several identities approve the same fraudulent work, a later audit can slash their stakes and bar them from future jobs. Splitting one attacker into many accounts therefore does not create free influence: every account needs capital at risk, and colluding accounts can lose it together. An atlas of prior audit outcomes, an opal badge for verified work, and crystal-clear slash rules help participants assess the risk.
